reference.title: Set the site up from opend.config.yaml
reference.shortdesc: The site block of opend.config.yaml declares how the hosted site is set up: who may read it, which versions readers can pick, how releases group into lines and which branches publish. With it, installing the GitHub App is the only step a person takes.

section.title: Fields
section.p: Every field is optional and takes the same values as the admin API. A field the block sets belongs to the repository; a field it leaves out stays yours to manage in the admin console.

property.propvalue: branch and tag patterns, such as [main, 'v*'] or ['docs/*']
property.propdesc: The release branches and tags on Docs source (releaseRefs of POST /admin/api/repos). Quote patterns that start with *. A branch it newly matches builds on its next push.
What anonymous visitors of a public site see (). The version may be latest. Products and features must be declared under attributes.

property.propvalue: {mode: off}, reader, fixed with version, list with versions, or live

section.p: opend validate checks the block like the rest of the file: an unknown field, a bad value or an undeclared product is an invalid-config error naming the field, such as site.access: Invalid option.

example.title: Example: a manual published per minor version
example.p: Docs in manual/, one docs/0.23-style branch per minor version, public with the free plan's content, and a version menu of every live line:
example.codeblock: title: Product Manual release: '0.23' map: maps/manual.ditamap attributes: product: [free, lite, business, enterprise, self-host] site: releaseRefs: ['docs/*'] releaseLines: minor access: public publicEntitlements: { products: [free], version: latest } versionPicker: { mode: live }

section.title: Which build's block applies
section.p: A build that goes live on the site's newest release line (the highest version, such as 0.23 next to 0.22) applies its block, in the same transaction that makes it live: no reader is ever served the new release under the old settings. Builds of older lines, such as a fix pushed to docs/0.22, and builds a newer push already replaced change nothing, so the settings never go back to an older branch's. Every change is in the audit log as repo:opend.config.yaml, with the branch and commit it came from, and every replica drops its cached pages at once.
Settings the block leaves out keep their values. Removing the block, or a field from it, hands the setting back to the console with its last value.

section.title: In the admin console
section.p: Settings the repository declares show Set by opend.config.yaml on Site & access and Docs source, with the branch and commit, and are read-only. The admin API answers 409 to a change to one of them, and a seed file leaves them as they are. To change one, change the repository.
A repository's settings are trusted like its content: anyone who can push to a release branch can make the site public. Protect those branches on GitHub (required reviews) if that matters.

section.title: Connecting the repository by itself
section.p: When the site has no docs source yet and the GitHub App can access exactly one repository, the site connects it without anyone choosing it:

ul.li: the release branches are its site.releaseRefs, or the default branch;
every release branch's head is queued to build, and the first build applies the rest of the block.

section.p: It happens when the installation completes (GitHub's return to the site, or the hosting provider's), on the next visit to the admin console's Overview or Docs source, on the first push from the repository, and on each poll of a site that polls. With several repositories, several candidate folders, or an invalid site block, nothing is connected: the Overview says why and Docs source offers the picker as before.
